$comment: PROPOSED vectors for CR-F / §11.26, to be merged into contract/schema/tests/vectors.json's `cases` array by the contract lane. Authored by the oracle lane 2026-08-29. EVERY CASE CITES THE §11.26 CLAUSE IT TESTS AND IS DERIVED FROM THE RULING TEXT, not from this lane's server -- the direction §8 requires. Field values are plausible literals; the shape is what is under test. Each `fail` perturbs its neighbouring `pass` in EXACTLY ONE way the cited clause forbids.

cases.why: §11.26 M1/M2/M3 — the whole-answer case: a sprite owned by a live slot, with world from the unbiased camera.
§11.26 M2 — THE RING CLICK the ruling names as a required vector. Owner word 0x0001; no slot, because a ring is not an object slot.

§11.26 M2 — RED-FIRST for the ring click: `slot` is present iff kind == 'object'. This is the exact defect the method exists to prevent — rebasing the 0x0001 sentinel into a plausible slot index and naming an object that did not draw the sprite. Perturbs the pass above by adding `slot` and nothing else.
§11.26 M2 — UNRESOLVABLE OWNER TABLE, the shape half: the loaded build has no Sprite_Owner, so there is no slot and no word was read.

§11.26 M2/M5 — RED-FIRST: with no owner table there was no word to read, so a `raw` here is a fabricated reading of memory that was never consulted. Perturbs the pass above by adding `raw` and nothing else.
§11.26 M3 — UNRESOLVABLE CAMERA, the third vector the ruling names: worldSource is independent of the owner half, so the owner answer still stands while `world` is absent.

§11.26 M3 — RED-FIRST for the camera: `world` present iff worldSource == 'camera'. A world beside 'unavailable' is a coordinate nobody computed, which is the silent-wrong-place failure M3 exists to stop. Perturbs the pass above by adding `world` and nothing else.
§11.26 M1/M2 — a non-sprite winner: no spriteIndex, and the owner table answered 'no owner'. Distinguishes `none` (table read, answer no) from `unavailable` (no table) in the vector set itself.
§11.26 M1 — RED-FIRST: `spriteIndex` is present iff the winner is a sprite, since it mirrors pixel_attribution's winner exactly. Perturbs the pass above by adding spriteIndex and nothing else.
§11.26 M1 — params are x, y in pixel_attribution's native-dot space with the same bounds.
§2.5 / §8 item 22 — an undeclared top-level param is -32602. M1 declares x and y only.
